chunks: Hammad, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you doubt, so you do not know whether you are in the third or in the second, or in the first, or in the fourth, so repeat and do not continue upon the doubt.
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they doubt which unit of prayer they are in during salat?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'breaking the doubt' (kharaj al-shakk) by requiring a full prayer repetition when the specific rak'ah is unknown, prioritizing certainty over the assumption of validity. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on caution (ihtiyat) in acts of worship, ensuring the prayer is not rendered void by lingering uncertainty. The directive underscores the spiritual discipline of recognizing one's state of worship rather than proceeding blindly.

en.hubeali: Hammad, from Ibn Abu Yafour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When you doubt, so you do not know whether you are in the third (Rak’at) or in the second, or in the first, or in the fourth, so repeat and do not continue upon the doubt’.
en.sarwar: 3. Hammad has narrated from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If you doubt and do not know if you have performed three or two or one or four, perform Salah (prayer) again and do not continue with doubt.’”
